data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：视频编辑器的功能、设计目标及用户需求

不同观点：
• Uehreka认为，要信任一个视频编辑器，必须展示其处理复杂项目的能力，例如30分钟时间线、多段1080p视频文件、每个轨道至少一个效果。他强调即使对初学者而言，编辑器也需要具备处理大文件和不良编辑习惯的能力，而不是仅针对初学者简化功能。他还建议不要从头开始构建编辑器，而应借鉴Cursor的成功经验，利用现有UX和插件生态。

• vivzkestrel提出了一种创新的想法，希望有语音控制或手势控制的视频编辑器，完全摆脱鼠标和键盘操作。这种方法虽然新颖，但目前市场上似乎没有此类产品，可能因为技术实现难度较大。

• Mr_Eri_Atlov对编辑器的简单使用体验表示满意，但提出增加图像居中功能的需求，以改善不同尺寸图像的处理。

• ojr认为市场上已有许多类似视频编辑器，主张开发移动端优先的视频编辑器，而非网页版，并指出需要与Capcut等现有免费桌面应用竞争。

• xnx和microflash则关注该编辑器与其他类似应用（如Omniclip和OpenCut）的比较，希望了解其独特优势。

• sitkack建议预先填充进行中的编辑时间线，让用户可以直接上手体验。

• leptons对编辑器中即将推出的AI功能持怀疑态度，认为AI并非必要，可能分散开发者对核心目标的注意力。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于视频编辑器的设计目标，一部分人认为应专注于复杂项目处理能力（Uehreka），另一部分人则希望看到创新功能（vivzkestrel）。
• 对AI功能的必要性存在分歧，leptons认为AI可能分散注意力，而其他评论未直接涉及此功能。
• 市场竞争和平台选择（网页端 vs 移动端）也是讨论的重要方面，ojr特别强调移动端的重要性。

data.title: Content-Aware Spaced Repetition
data.author: ran3000
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了间隔重复系统（SRS）中的**内容感知记忆模型**，指出现有系统仅根据复习历史安排卡片，忽略卡片内容的语义关联。传统SRS将每张卡片视为独立单元，不理解相关内容应共同强化记忆。作者提出**内容感知模型**不仅提高调度准确性，还能实现更灵活智能的学习工具，如多角度测试理解的系统或与语音AI导师对话的学习体验。

文章进一步区分了**调度器**和**记忆模型**的概念。调度器决定今天复习哪些卡片，而记忆模型预测学生记住某张卡片的概率。经典的SuperMemo SM-2调度器简单有效，但现代算法如SM-18和FSRS通过记忆模型优化了复习安排。内容感知模型有望改变学习体验，但面临数据和用户体验设计上的挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：间隔重复系统（SRS）的优化与应用

不同观点：
• barrell认为，虽然FSRS比SM-2算法略有改进，但这种改进在实际使用中几乎不易察觉。他强调，SRS的真正突破在于应用层面的创新，例如通过改善用户体验来提高学习的吸引力，而不是仅仅关注算法本身的微小提升。
• joshdavham指出，FSRS目前是内容无关和牌组无关的，这使得它易于集成，但同时也意味着模型可能会有些欠拟合。他建议通过为不同主题优化单独的FSRS模型，或者引入一些牌组相关的特性来改进。
• mabster提到了ebisu这个使用贝叶斯统计的SRS系统，并建议通过优化句子中单词的呈现顺序来提高学习效率。
• ran3000认为，SRS模型的技术改进不仅能提高调度准确性，还能解锁更好的产品用户体验和新型SRS。
• jeffalyanak介绍了AnkiMorphs工具，它通过分析句子中的词素来重新排序新卡片，从而提高学习效率。
• kebsup对SRS算法的优化持怀疑态度，认为过于精确的算法可能会导致卡片感觉过于困难或简单，主张混合难易卡片可能是一个特性而非缺陷。
• rahimnathwani提到了一个Anki插件，它尝试增加“兄弟”卡片之间的间隔。
• huhtenberg强调了将来自同一信息的卡片视为一组的重要性，批评Anki没有支持这一点。
• HDMI_Cable指出构建内容感知记忆模型面临的主要挑战是缺乏数据，并建议与AnKing等预制牌组制作者合作获取数据。
• vhrrsrivr提出了一种通过卡片本身定义概念关系的方法，而不是依赖于嵌入空间。
• charcircuit希望内容感知的调度器不要将相似卡片放在一起，以免混淆。
• daft_pink对其他用于AI驱动语音的间隔重复软件感兴趣，希望了解市场上的其他选项。
• pessimizer建议不要分析卡片语义，而是通过观察卡片一起通过或失败的情况来构建卡片之间的关系图。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个SRS工具和插件，如AnkiMorphs、ebisu和Anki插件，展示了现有工具的多样性和可扩展性。
• 对内容感知和牌组感知的讨论揭示了SRS系统在个性化和优化学习体验方面的潜力。
• 争议的焦点在于SRS算法优化的实际效果和必要性，部分用户认为微小的算法改进不如应用层面的创新重要。
• 数据缺乏被认为是构建更智能SRS模型的一个主要障碍，合作获取数据被建议为可能的解决方案。

44790422.article_content:
Giacomo Randazzo
2025-08-04
Content-aware Spaced Repetition
Spaced repetition systems are powerful, but they have a fundamental blind spot: they don’t understand what your flashcards are
about
.
To your SRS, a card asking “what’s the capital of Italy?” and another asking “what country is Rome the capital of?” are treated independently, each with its own isolated review history. It has no concept that reviewing related material should reinforce your memory of the whole topic.
At the heart of every SRS is a
memory model
which predicts how long you’ll remember each card based on your past performance. Most of today’s models ignore the
content
of the cards entirely. This is where
content-aware memory models
come in: they account for the semantic meaning of your cards, not just your review ratings.
This is more than a minor tweak for scheduling accuracy. It’s a foundational change that makes it practical to build the fluid, intelligent learning tools many have envisioned: from
idea-centric memory systems
that test understanding from multiple angles to truly
conversational spaced repetition
with a voice-enabled AI agent as tutor.
This post explores what content-aware memory models are, and the new kinds of learning experiences they make possible.
Contents
Schedulers and memory models
Content-aware memory models
KARL
Small experiments on Rember data
Other considerations
UX unlocks
Data problem
Schedulers and memory models
I find it useful to distinguish between schedulers and memory models. This distinction wasn’t immediately obvious to me when I first approached the topic, but I’ve found it essential for thinking clearly about spaced repetition systems (SRS). Here, I’ll introduce both concept and I’ll make the case that separating schedulers from memory models enables independent innovation and simplifies the development of each component by isolating user experience (UX) concerns within the scheduler. In the literature, the scheduler is sometimes called the “teacher model” since it decides what to teach, while the memory model is the “student model” since it represents what the student knows.
In Anki and other spaced repetition systems, the
scheduler
is an algorithm that picks the next card to review today, answering the question
“Given the review history of every card in the student’s collection, which cards should the student review in this session?”
. In practice, when building a spaced repetition system, this is the question you actually care about. The scheduler’s core job is deciding
which cards to show today
, not just
when each card should ideally be reviewed
. A card might be “due” for review, but the scheduler might skip it due to daily review limits, prioritize other overdue cards, or defer it based on other goals.
For a long time, the only scheduler available in Anki was
a variant of SuperMemo’s SM-2 scheduler
, which dates back to
1987
. It’s remarkably simple yet effective. SuperMemo has since advanced its scheduler, now at version
SM-18
. The latest iterations of the algorithm achieve the same retention levels with fewer reviews, and are more robust when reviews deviate from optimal intervals, for example when a student returns from a break of several weeks. While the SuperMemo schedulers are closed-source, an explanation of how they work is
available
.
FSRS
is an open-source scheduler by Jarrett Ye built on similar principles to modern SuperMemo algorithms and can be used in Anki.
A
memory model
predicts forgetting curves, answering the question
“Given the review history of every card in the student’s collection, what are the chances the student remembers a specific card at any given moment?”
We define
retrievability
as the probability that a student remembers a card at a particular time. In practice, we often model this as a binary outcome where a student either remembers or forgets a card. Some spaced repetition systems allow for more nuanced grading. For example, Anki has four options: “Again”, “Hard”, “Good”, “Easy”. This additional information from the review history can be used to make memory models more accurate.
The forgetting curve plots this retrievability over time. A memory model’s job is to compute these curves based on a student’s review history. Retrievability generally decreases over time, as it becomes more likely that the student will forget the card. For example, here are the forgetting curves estimated by different memory models from the same review history (the figure comes from my
master’s thesis
):
The relationship between schedulers and memory models varies across different systems. A scheduler may or may not use a memory model. For example, the
Leitner system
and SM-2 do not rely on a memory model to schedule reviews, they are based on simple mechanical rules. Modern schedulers like SM-18 and FSRS instead include a memory model (stability and difficulty are used to compute retrievability). I recommend taking a look at Fernando Borretti’s articles on the implementing
SM-2

data.title: What Can a Cell Remember?
data.author: chapulin
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了单个细胞是否能够记忆和学习，挑战了传统上认为记忆和学习仅依赖于多细胞神经系统的观点。作者提到，遗传学家芭芭拉·麦克林托克在1983年诺贝尔奖演讲中提出“细胞对自己了解多少”的问题，引发了后续研究。近年来，科学家发现，即使是单细胞生物和人体内无神经的细胞，也能记录和响应过去的经验。例如，纽约大学的科学家展示肾脏细胞能够“记住”定期呈现的化学信号模式。这种“无神经”记忆现象表明，细胞可能比我们想象的更具认知能力，记忆可能在神经系统出现之前就已存在，对所有生物都有用。研究这些单细胞的记忆机制，可能为我们理解记忆提供新视角。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于黏菌（如Physarum polycephalum）是否具有记忆能力以及单细胞生物的学习与记忆机制的讨论。

不同观点：
• [ravenstine] 认为黏菌的记忆可能超越了仅依赖其留下的黏液路径。他通过自己培养的Physarum polycephalum观察到，黏菌在多次接受某种食物后，会突然拒绝再次接受该食物，暗示其可能具有某种程度的“记忆”。

• [BiraIgnacio] 引入了Assembly Theory，认为该理论可以解释这种现象，暗示无需假设黏菌具有记忆能力。

• [userbinator] 表示自己因为其他新闻的影响，对讨论产生了不同的理解，特别是关于连接电话的联想，显示出讨论的背景可能影响解读。

• [the-mitr] 引用了John Tyler Bonner的著作《The Evolution of Culture in Animals》，提出关于单细胞生物是否可以学习、记忆和形成文化的思考，扩展了对学习和文化传承的理解。

• [kylehotchkiss] 反对将细胞行为拟人化，认为细胞对刺激的反应仅仅是由于它们具有相应的受体，而非真正的“记忆”或学习能力，将细胞视为“小机器”更为合理。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于单细胞生物如黏菌是否具有记忆能力，以及这种能力是否可以被视为一种学习或文化传承。
• 不同评论者引用了个人观察、科学理论和文献资料来支持各自的观点，显示出该问题具有多角度的探讨空间。
• 讨论还涉及到如何定义和理解记忆与学习，以及在何种程度上可以将这些概念应用于非高等生物。

I
n 1983, the octogenarian geneticist Barbara McClintock stood at the lectern of the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm. She was famously publicity averse — nearly a hermit — but it’s customary for people to speak when they’re awarded a Nobel Prize, so she delivered a halting account of the experiments that had led to her discovery, in the early 1950s, of how DNA sequences can relocate across the genome. Near the end of the speech, blinking through wire-framed glasses, she changed the subject, asking: “What does a cell know of itself?”
McClintock had a reputation for eccentricity. Still, her question seemed more likely to come from a philosopher than a plant geneticist. She went on to describe lab experiments in which she had seen plant cells respond in a “thoughtful manner.” Faced with unexpected stress, they seemed to adjust in ways that were “beyond our present ability to fathom.” What does a cell know of itself? It would be the work of future biologists, she said, to find out.
Forty years later, McClintock’s question hasn’t lost its potency. Some of those future biologists are now hard at work unpacking what “knowing” might mean for a single cell, as they hunt for signs of basic cognitive phenomena — like the ability to remember and learn — in unicellular creatures and nonneural human cells alike. Science has long taken the view that a multicellular nervous system is a prerequisite for such abilities, but new research is revealing that single cells, too, keep a record of their experiences for what appear to be adaptive purposes.
Barbara McClintock
Science History Images
In a provocative study published in
Nature Communications
late last year, the neuroscientist Nikolay Kukushkin and his mentor Thomas J. Carew at New York University showed that human kidney cells growing in a dish can
“remember” patterns of chemical signals
when they’re presented at regularly spaced intervals — a memory phenomenon common to all animals, but unseen outside the nervous system until now. Kukushkin is part of a small but enthusiastic cohort of researchers studying “aneural,” or brainless, forms of memory. What does a cell know of itself? So far, their research suggests that the answer to McClintock’s question might be: much more than you think.
Brainless Learning
The prevailing wisdom in neuroscience has long been that memory and learning are consequences of “synaptic plasticity” in the brain. The connections between clusters of neurons simultaneously active during an experience strengthen into networks that remain active even after the experience has passed, perpetuating it as a memory. This phenomenon, expressed by the adage “Neurons that fire together, wire together,” has shaped our understanding of memory for the better part of a century. But if solitary nonneural cells can also remember and learn, then networks of neurons can’t be the whole story.
From an evolutionary perspective, it makes sense for cells outside a nervous system to be changed by their experiences in ways that encourage survival. “Memory is something that’s useful to all living systems, including systems that predated the emergence of the brain by hundreds of millions of years,” said
Sam Gershman
, a cognitive scientist at Harvard University.
Acellular slime molds, foraging for food, lay down chemical traces that remind them where they’ve been. Bacteria compare present and previous conditions as they move through chemical gradients towards more favorable environments. Gershman has a hunch that these “more ancient form[s] of memory” may play an important, complementary role to synaptic plasticity — so much so that he recently added a wet lab to his operation to systematically study the single-celled ciliate
Stentor coeruleus
.
Ciliates might sound like an unconventional focus for a cognitive scientist, but the study of memory in these unicellular creatures dates back to the early 20th century. The zoologist Herbert Spencer Jennings, in his
Behavior of the Lower Organisms
,
detailed experiments
with a similar ciliate,
S. roeselii
, as early as 1906
.
Found in freshwater ponds around the world, these trumpet-shaped cells anchor themselves to their environment with a sticky “holdfast” and draw in floating food particles by beating hairli
44749211.article_summary: 文章探讨了单个细胞是否能够记忆和学习，挑战了传统上认为记忆和学习仅依赖于多细胞神经系统的观点。作者提到，遗传学家芭芭拉·麦克林托克在1983年诺贝尔奖演讲中提出“细胞对自己了解多少”的问题，引发了后续研究。近年来，科学家发现，即使是单细胞生物和人体内无神经的细胞，也能记录和响应过去的经验。例如，纽约大学的科学家展示肾脏细胞能够“记住”定期呈现的化学信号模式。这种“无神经”记忆现象表明，细胞可能比我们想象的更具认知能力，记忆可能在神经系统出现之前就已存在，对所有生物都有用。研究这些单细胞的记忆机制，可能为我们理解记忆提供新视角。
44749211.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于黏菌（如Physarum polycephalum）是否具有记忆能力以及单细胞生物的学习与记忆机制的讨论。

不同观点：
• [ravenstine] 认为黏菌的记忆可能超越了仅依赖其留下的黏液路径。他通过自己培养的Physarum polycephalum观察到，黏菌在多次接受某种食物后，会突然拒绝再次接受该食物，暗示其可能具有某种程度的“记忆”。

• [BiraIgnacio] 引入了Assembly Theory，认为该理论可以解释这种现象，暗示无需假设黏菌具有记忆能力。

• [userbinator] 表示自己因为其他新闻的影响，对讨论产生了不同的理解，特别是关于连接电话的联想，显示出讨论的背景可能影响解读。

• [the-mitr] 引用了John Tyler Bonner的著作《The Evolution of Culture in Animals》，提出关于单细胞生物是否可以学习、记忆和形成文化的思考，扩展了对学习和文化传承的理解。

• [kylehotchkiss] 反对将细胞行为拟人化，认为细胞对刺激的反应仅仅是由于它们具有相应的受体，而非真正的“记忆”或学习能力，将细胞视为“小机器”更为合理。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于单细胞生物如黏菌是否具有记忆能力，以及这种能力是否可以被视为一种学习或文化传承。
• 不同评论者引用了个人观察、科学理论和文献资料来支持各自的观点，显示出该问题具有多角度的探讨空间。
• 讨论还涉及到如何定义和理解记忆与学习，以及在何种程度上可以将这些概念应用于非高等生物。

data.title: Show HN: Sidequest.js – Background jobs for Node.js using your database
data.author: merencia
data.article_summary:
这篇文章是一个Sidequest.js的快速入门指南，帮助在Node.js应用中设置Sidequest.js。主要步骤包括：

1. **安装**：按照安装指南安装Sidequest.js，建议使用默认的SQLite后端驱动。
2. **创建任务**：定义一个`Job`类，如`EmailJob`，定制任务行为。
3. **启动Sidequest**：配置并启动Sidequest引擎，可以使用默认设置并启用仪表板。
4. **加入任务队列**：将任务加入队列，如`EmailJob`，等待处理。
5. **查看仪表板**：访问http://localhost:8678查看任务状态和管理仪表板。

完成这些步骤后，可以进一步探索高级功能，如自定义任务类、管理队列、配置引擎和使用仪表板。更多详细信息可查阅完整文档。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Sidequest工具的功能、使用场景及其与其他工具的比较

不同观点：
• **Kristianc** 对LGPL许可要求及其对下游用户重新链接的合规性提出质疑，特别是在Sidequest与后端基础设施紧密集成的情况下，如何满足许可要求存在疑问。
• **Sleiben** 对使用Kubernetes（k8s）和12factor设计模式的场景进行了讨论，并询问是否应使用Sidequest替代当前的cron job和监控方案，尤其是对DataDog的观察能力有所顾虑。
• **Spiffytech** 对Sidequest的仪表盘功能表示赞赏，认为这对于需要持久化任务队列的较大项目非常有用，并指出许多其他任务队列库缺乏管理工具。
• **Drewrbaker** 表示对Sidequest感兴趣，但指出其使用的Postgres on Supabase不支持事务锁定，可能限制了其使用。
• **Seymon** 将Sidequest与Graphile Worker进行比较，询问二者之间的差异和选择建议。
• **Anonzzzies** 对Sidequest不依赖Redis或Postgres表示赞赏，因为其项目不使用这些数据库技术。

补充讨论：
• **MutedEstate45** 关注Sidequest在使用Postgres时的性能问题，尤其是当工作线程与OLTP流量竞争时，询问Sidequest是否采用与Oban类似的建议锁机制或其它节流策略。
• **Stephenlf** 和 **Drewbitt** 对Sidequest使用SQLite而非Redis表示赞赏，并提到了与pg-boss和hatchet等其他工具的比较，认为根据项目需求，Sidequest是一个不错的选择。
• **Nip** 对Sidequest与pg-boss进行了直接比较，希望获得开发者的意见以便在即将进行的项目中做出选择。
• **Shireboy** 作为.NET开发者，寻找Hangfire的替代品，认为Sidequest是一个理想的解决方案。
• **Mousetree** 是一个Rails的ActiveJob用户，表示Sidequest满足了其在Node.js中实现类似功能的需求。
• **Hersko** 简单表达了对Sidequest的兴趣和赞赏。

争议焦点：
• Sidequest在使用Postgres时的性能和事务锁定问题（Drewrbaker, MutedEstate45）。
• Sidequest与类似工具（如Graphile Worker和pg-boss）的比较和选择（Seymon, Nip）。
• LGPL许可要求对下游用户的影响及合规性问题（Kristianc）。

44787343.article_content:
Quick Start Guide
​
This guide will help you quickly set up Sidequest.js in your Node.js application.
1. Installation
​
To install Sidequest.js, check out
Installation Guide
. If you are strictly following this quick start, you should install the SQLite backend driver, which is the default backend for Sidequest.js.
2. Job Creation
​
The first step is to create a
Job
class. This class will define the job's behavior and can be customized as needed.
typescript
// jobs/EmailJob.js
import
{ Job }
from
"sidequest"
;
export
class
EmailJob
extends
Job
{
async
run
(
to
,
subject
,
body
) {
console.
log
(
`Sending email to ${
to
}: ${
subject
}`
);
// Your email sending logic here
return
{ sent:
true
, timestamp:
new
Date
() };
}
}
3. Sidequest Startup
​
The next step is to configure and start the
Sidequest engine
. You can use the default settings or customize it according to your needs.
typescript
// app.js
import
{ Sidequest }
from
"sidequest"
;
// Quick start Sidequest with default settings and Dashboard enabled
await
Sidequest.
start
();
console.
log
(
"Sidequest started! Dashboard: http://localhost:8678"
);
4. Enqueue Jobs
​
Now that you have your job class and Sidequest is running, you can
enqueue jobs
to be processed.
typescript
// Somewhere in your application
import
{ Sidequest }
from
"sidequest"
;
import
{ EmailJob }
from
"./jobs/EmailJob.js"
;
// Simple job
await
Sidequest.
build
(EmailJob).
enqueue
(
"user@example.com"
,
"Welcome!"
,
"Thanks for signing up!"
);
5. Check the Dashboard
​
You can access the
Sidequest Dashboard
at
http://localhost:8678
to monitor your jobs, queues, and their statuses. The dashboard provides a user-friendly interface to manage and visualize your job processing.
What's Next?
​
Now that you have a basic setup, you can explore more advanced features like:
Learn about
Jobs
and how to create custom job classes
Learn about
Queues
and how to manage them
Learn how to configure and run the
Sidequest Engine
Check
Sidequest's Dashboard
for monitoring and managing jobs
Check the rest of the documentation for detailed guides on these topics.

data.title: Thingino: Open-Source Firmware for IP Cameras
data.author: zakki
data.article_summary: 这篇文章列出了各种支持Thingino固件的IP摄像头型号及其硬件细节，包括SoC、图像传感器、Wi-Fi模块和闪存芯片大小。由于制造商可能在不通知的情况下更改硬件，因此这些参数必须匹配才能获得支持。文章详细列出了室内、灯泡形和室外IP摄像头的具体型号和硬件配置，例如360 AP1PA3、AJCloud T-CP2011-W32A、Eufy C120、Wyze Cam Pan 2等。还提供了安装指导链接和相关资源，如GitHub仓库、Discord服务器和Telegram群组。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenIPC和thingino开源固件的应用及相关技术讨论

不同观点：
• 一些用户如[cnst]和[tmjwid]对thingino固件表示支持，强调了其在老旧摄像头上的易用性和性能提升。例如，[tmjwid]提到其在Wyze摄像头上的升级过程顺利，并赞赏了其夜视功能的改进。
• [glonq]和[1024core]则关注其对特定品牌摄像头（如Yi和Wyze）的支持情况及实际应用效果，尤其是对广告和应用兼容性的不满。
• [Roark66]指出该项目缺乏基本的AI运动检测和警报功能，认为这是其不足之处。
• [zakki]和[2bluesc]提供了技术细节和资源链接，帮助其他用户更好地理解和使用thingino固件。
• [rcarmo]则关注到HomeKit支持的缺失，并提到其之前使用ESP32摄像头的经验。
• [aag01]作为开发贡献者之一，分享了其组合使用多种工具构建家庭监控系统的经验，并表示对thingino的支持。

补充讨论：
• [harel]表示对该项目的存在感到高兴，并分享了成功修复旧摄像头的个人经验。
• [lammylamy]提到在尝试刷机过程中遇到的问题，如Wyze2摄像头变砖。
• [zakki]在最后提出了对开源自托管视频录制和处理工具的推荐需求。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在功能上的不足，特别是AI运动检测和应用兼容性（如HomeKit支持）方面。
• 用户对广告干扰的不满和开源固件带来的实际改进形成对比。

总体来看，讨论围绕thingino固件的技术实现、实际应用效果及功能扩展的可能性展开，既有正面支持的声音，也有对其不足之处的批评和建议。

主要讨论点：针对EconTeen这一金融教育平台的评论和争议

不同观点：
• 认为该平台可能是为了赚钱而仓促推出，内容价值存疑。
  - 例子：有人指出没有确认该学习材料是否有用，且有很多免费资源可供使用（[lelanthran]）。

  - 例子：有人通过自己玩网络游戏的经验，认为实际的“利益相关”对学习金融知识很重要，平台可能缺乏这一点（[hirvi74]）。

• 对订阅模式的批评，建议使用书籍等传统教育方式。

• 对平台透明度和课程内容不明确的批评。

  - 例子：有人直观反应是需要这个教育的青少年可能没有能力支付费用（[_def]）。

  - 例子：有人在移动端浏览FAQ时无法滚动答案部分（[theogravity]）。

data.title: 3D Line Drawings
data.author: tansh
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何通过增强3D高斯溅射（3D Gaussian Splatting）技术生成3D线条图。作者Amritansh Kwatra描述了利用Chan等人的方法，将照片转换为传达几何和语义信息的线条图，并结合3D高斯溅射生成实时辐射场渲染。具体方法是将原始图像替换为根据Chan等人的模型生成的线条图，然后进行3D高斯溅射处理。这一过程可以在两个阶段进行：在结构自运动（SfM）计算相机姿态和稀疏点之前，或在训练3D高斯溅射之前。最终生成的3D线条图根据视角变化，类似于传统素描效果，且保留了一定的颜色信息。

44792441.article_content:
Creating 3D Line Drawings
Amritansh Kwatra
June 30th, 2025
This is an experiment examing how to create a 3D line drawing of a scene. In this post, I will describe how this can be done by augmenting the process of generating
3D Gaussian Splats
3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering
, by Kerbl et al.
and leveraging a process to transform photographs into
Informative Line Drawings
Learning to Generate Line Drawings that Convey Geometry and Semantics
, by Chan, Isola & Durand
.
Examples
The majority of scenes shown above are generated using a
contour
style.
You can switch the active scene using the menu in the top-right corner of the iframe
. Each scene is trained for 21,000 iterations on an Nvidia RTX 4080S, using
gaussian-splatting-cuda
from MrNerf with default settings. Examples here were generated using scenes from the
Tanks & Temples Benchmark
. The scene is interactive, and rendered using
Mark Kellogg's web-based renderer
.
To explore these scenes in fullscreen,
click here.
How it works
Creating Line Drawings from Images
⊕
Figure 1.
(a)
A source image from the Caterpillar scene in
Tanks & Temples
.
(b)
A generated line drawing in the
contour
style.
(c)
A generated line drawing in the
anime
style.
Images are transformed into line drawings using the approach introduced by Chan et al. in
Learning to Generate Line Drawings that Convey Geometry and Semantics
. They describe a process for transforming photographs into line drawings that preserve the semantics and geometry captured in the photograph while rendering the image in an artistic style. They do this by training a generative adversarial network (GAN) that minimizes
geometry
The geometry loss is computed using monocular depth estimation.
,
semantics
The semantics loss is computed using CLIP embeddings.
, and
appearance
The appearance loss is based on a collection of unpaired style references.
losses. Their work is fantastic and I recommend reading their paper if you're interested in the details. Figure 1 depicts the input photograph and output line drawing in two styles, generated using Chan et al.'s
code and model weights
.
3D Gaussian Splatting
3D Gaussian Splatting is a technique that transforms collections of
posed images
Images for which we estimate the relative position and rotation of the camera in the scene. Usually, this is computed using Structure-from-Motion (SfM).
into a volumetric representation called a radiance field. Generally, scenes can be created from collections of images captured from multiple overlapping viewpoints, either by taking multiple photographs from different angles or by sampling an input video while moving through the scene. For more complete details on 3D Gaussian Splatting, I encourage you to read
the paper
or watch this
explanation video
from Computerphile.
The scenes that are produced using 3D Gaussian Splatting are photorealistic and can be rendered at real-time rates using existing tools such as WebGL. However, I noticed that if the images used to train the 3D Gaussian Splat were swapped out with the
line-drawing counterparts
While I transformed the images into line drawings, this transformation could be carried out using a number of other stylistic effects.
then the resulting scene would depict a kind of 3D line drawing. Similar to
regular sketching
Illustrating a 3D scene as a 2D drawing from a specific perspective.
, the lines that are rendered are view-dependant and change based on your perspective in the scene.
Swapping Source Images
⊕
Figure 2.
The transformed images can be used to create 3D line drawings by swapping them for the original images in one of two places, shown here in green. Either before using SfM to generate the sparse model and camera poses or prior to training the 3D Gaussian Splat. The former computes SfM points based on the transformed images, while the latter keeps the points from the original images and computes the rendering loss using the transformed images. Figure adapted from the
original 3D Gaussian Splatting paper
.
Generating these 3D line drawings requires only a slight modification to the conventional process for generating 3D Gaussian Splats. At a high level, we simply swap the original images with the ones generated using Chan et al.'s method for transforming images into informative line drawings. This swap can happen in two places: prior to training the 3D Gaussian Splat or prior to estimating camera poses and sparse points using structure-from-motion (SfM).
When images are transformed prior to training the 3D Gaussian Splat, the camera poses and initial 3D Gaussians are derived from the original images but the loss is computed by comparing the rasterization output to the informative line drawing. As a result, the final scene also captures slight amounts of color that is not present in the transformed images. I believe this is a side-effect of intializing the 3D Gaussians using the original images. If you transform the images prior to applying SfM, the ini

主要讨论点：预付费信用是否应有过期规则及其合理性

不同观点：
• **反对信用过期**：
   - [backprop1989] 提到其公司购买的大量非过期信用不能算作收入，导致会计问题。
   - [gloosx] 批评Anthropic不允许移除信用卡，认为公司贪婪。
   - [verdverm] 主张按使用量计费并允许设置限额，而非预付费模式。
   - [pzo] 提到Anthropic和OpenAI都存在类似问题，且年化 inflation 极高。
   - [blindriver] 认为在加州这种做法可能不合法，类比礼品证书不能过期的法律。
   - [peteforde] 指出Audible等其他服务也有类似过期规则，令人不满。

• **支持或理解信用过期**：
   - [freedomben] 认为Anthropic明确展示了过期规则，不算隐瞒，尽管个人不喜欢这种做法。
   - [ranguna] 提到购买时已明确告知信用会过期，并建议少存勤充以减少损失。
   - [aldousd666] 分享个人经验，因过期压力首次使用服务，认为这种机制有推动作用。

• **中立或普遍化观点**：
   - [just-ok] 指出OpenAI也有类似做法，个人曾因此吃过亏。
   - [ChrisMarshallNY] 认为这是普遍现象，例如Shutterstock也有信用过期规则。
   - [copypaper] 提出是否可以通过管理自动充值来避免信用过期问题。
   - [sometimes_all] 强调这不是Anthropic独有的做法，大多数LLM提供商（如OpenAI和Perplexity）都有类似规则，且在购买前已明确说明。

补充讨论：
- **法律与合规性**：[blindriver] 质疑Anthropic信用过期在加州的合法性。
- **消费者体验**：多个评论提到对信用过期的不满，尤其在未使用服务的情况下被收费。
- **实用建议**：[ranguna] 和 [copypaper] 建议通过减少预存金额和勤充值来降低损失风险。

争议焦点：预付费信用是否应有过期规则及其对消费者的公平性。

data.title: Using drone imagery and AI to rapidly assess damage after hurricanes and floods
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 德克萨斯农工大学开发的CLARKE系统利用无人机影像和人工智能，在几分钟内快速评估飓风和洪水后的损害情况。该系统由计算机科学与工程博士生Tom Manzini和救援机器人专家Robin Murphy博士领导开发，可以在短短七分钟内评估2000户住宅的损毁情况，帮助应急响应人员迅速制定救援计划。CLARKE使用先进的计算机视觉和机器学习算法，生成详细的损害报告和绕行路线，特别适用于农村或难以到达的地区。该系统已经过超过21,000栋房屋的训练，并在2024年飓风季成功部署于佛罗里达和宾夕法尼亚。其快速评估能力显著加速了救灾响应，被视为改变游戏规则的工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：该技术的应用范围及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• __rito__: 提到该技术让他想起在黑客松中快速开发的一个项目，他们微调了CLIP模型以处理卫星图像，并且推理速度非常快。他提供了项目链接，展示相关实现。
  
• drcode: 对文章标题表示质疑，认为该技术仅被用于灾难响应地图，而不能应用于其他类型地图，例如用于战争前线的地图。

• Oceoss: 提出无人机不仅在洪水监测中有用，在火灾监测中也可能非常有用。

• imoverclocked: 表示支持这类技术的发展，但同时指出，人们并没有解决未来几个世纪大多数自然灾害的根本原因，仅在应对表面问题。

• Mountain_Skies: 提到该技术还可以检测房屋的未经批准的改动，或者任何保险公司认为会增加财产风险的改动。

补充讨论：

• imoverclocked提出了对技术应用的更深层次思考，关注长期自然灾害的根源问题。

• 该技术是否仅限于灾难响应，还是可以扩展到其他领域，如战争前线地图或保险风险评估。
• 技术发展是否应更多关注解决自然灾害的根本原因，而不仅限于应急响应。

Science & Tech
AI Turns Drone Footage Into Disaster Response Maps In Minutes
A system developed at Texas A&M uses drone imagery and artificial intelligence to rapidly assess damage after hurricanes and floods, offering life-saving insights in minutes.
Jul 28, 2025
By
Lesley Henton
,
Texas A&M University Division of Marketing and Communications
4 min. read
CLARKE was trained on drone images from over 21,000 houses across 10 major disasters.
Credit: Texas A&M University College of Engineering
A tool developed at Texas A&M University is set to transform how emergency responders assess damage after disasters. The technology, known as CLARKE (Computer vision and Learning for Analysis of Roads and Key Edifices) uses artificial intelligence and drone imagery to evaluate damage to buildings, roads and other infrastructure in a matter of minutes.
CLARKE was created by a team of researchers led by Tom Manzini, a Ph.D. candidate in computer science and engineering, and
Dr. Robin Murphy
, a pioneer in the field of rescue robotics.
“This is the first AI system that can classify building and road damage from drone imagery at this scale and speed,” Murphy said. “We’re talking about assessing a neighborhood of 2,000 homes in just seven minutes. That kind of speed can save lives and resources.”
The system has already proven its value during the 2024 hurricane season, when it was deployed in Florida and Pennsylvania following Hurricanes Debby and Helene.
The Magic Of Machine Learning
The name CLARKE is a nod to science fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke’s quote: “Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic.” According to Murphy, the name was inspired by drone pilots working with the system who began calling its machine-learning capabilities “magic.”
But there’s nothing mystical about the science behind it. CLARKE uses cutting-edge computer vision and machine-learning algorithms to analyze drone footage, overlay damage assessments on maps, and generate spreadsheets listing each structure’s address and damage level. For roadways, it even includes a Google Maps-style route planner that helps responders avoid impassable roads.
CLARKE doesn’t just tell you what’s damaged, it tells you how to get around that damage. That’s critical when every second counts.
Dr. Robin Murphy
Senior Professor of Computer Science and Engineering
Texas A&M University College of Engineering
In rural or hard-to-reach areas, traditional damage assessments can take days, delaying aid and complicating logistics. With CLARKE, officials could launch drones and receive a comprehensive damage report within minutes, dramatically accelerating response times.
“Rural counties often have lost wireless connectivity so they can’t send imagery to state and federal agencies for manual inspection,” Murphy said. “CLARKE empowers them to take immediate action.”
The system was trained on drone images from over 21,000 houses across 10 major disasters, including Hurricanes Harvey and Ian. This extensive dataset allows CLARKE to recognize a wide range of damage patterns, making it adaptable to different types of disasters, including hurricanes, floods and wildfires.
Training The Front Lines
While the technology itself is groundbreaking, its success depends on the people using it. Last month, more than 60 emergency responders from 38 agencies and eight private companies gathered in Tallahassee, Florida, for a two-hour awareness training session on CLARKE. The event, hosted by Florida State University, was expected to draw 15 to 20 participants but ended up with nearly 100 registrations, highlighting the growing interest in AI-driven disaster tools.
David Merrick, program director of the Emergency Management and Homeland Security Program at Florida State University and task force lead for unmanned aerial systems for the state of Florida, praised the system’s capabilities.
“This is a game changer for rural counties — they can fly drones and then immediately understand the extent of damage in their area rather than wait days for the information from other sources,” Merrick said. “It will help make damage assessment more efficient and effective.”
An image from CLARKE, which can assess damage on 2,000 homes in seven minutes.
Credit: Texas A&M University College of Engineering
Looking Ahead
CLARKE’s development began in 2022, and its creators continue to refine the system based on real-world feedback. After its deployment in 2024, the Texas A&M team participated in a tabletop exercise hosted by the AI Institute for Societal Decision-Making at the Florida Office of Emergency Management in April 2025 to gather input from responders. That session not only generated valuable suggestions but also sparked demand for formal training, leading to the June event in Florida.
Murphy sees a bright future for CLARKE, both as a practical tool and as a platform for further research.

data.title: Where to find ideas
data.author: kiyanwang
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：寻找创业想法和解决问题的途径

不同观点：
• TrackerFF认为，大多数创业想法来自于在某些行业工作时接触到未解决的问题。他强调，很多创业者曾在科技行业或咨询行业工作，并发现未被解决的问题或未开发的市场。他指出，消费者通常只能看到B2C领域的问题，而B2B领域的问题往往被忽略。

• Wavemode强调，与潜在客户交谈并录制对话以审查反馈的重要性。他认为，通过描述未见过的产品来了解客户需求是不可靠的，实际的原型测试更为有效。

• Lyngbakr提出，成功的创业者不仅仅是空想，而是深入理解潜在客户的需求。他支持“解决自身问题”的建议，因为创业者本身就是潜在客户。

• Miggy建议通过观察不对称性来寻找创业想法。他指出，当某些事情对一些人来说很容易，而对另一些人却很难时，往往揭示了潜在的复杂性或缺失的工具，从而提供了创业机会。

• Cjs_ac认为，现代软件工程的核心在于如何表示问题的细节和解决方案，而不仅仅是编码。他强调深入领域知识的重要性，并建议离开大科技公司的生态系统，去小型公司寻找问题。

• Z0r提供了一个幽默的建议，通过视频链接让人们了解如何获取想法。

• Lelanthran简洁地指出，通过实际行动来发现想法。

• Secretsatan以讽刺的方式建议从下属那里窃取想法。

• Hollowonepl对创业指导持怀疑态度，认为很多创业想法只是为了吸引投资，最终可能导致更多问题。他质疑创业文化的真实价值。

• Antonkar提到一个声称规划了终极未来的案例，分享了创业想法。

• Andrewstuart建议关注社会、商业或技术变革以发现新的机会，并提到复制和改进优秀想法的策略。

• Boredemployee认为，现实中大多数人已经在解决问题，但成功往往依赖于运气、影响力、 networking和时机等因素。

• Begueradj指出，一些工作场所要求员工在特定会议上提出新想法，但未实施的想法是无价值的。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于创业想法的真实性和实现价值。一些评论者强调实际操作和原型测试的重要性，而另一些则质疑创业文化的实质和动机。
- 深入理解客户需求和行业问题被普遍认为是发现创业机会的关键。
- 不同背景（如科技行业、小型公司）的经验提供了多样的视角和方法。

data.article_summary: ClojureCivitas 是一个开放项目，旨在通过创建和分享 Clojure 相关内容来构建知识社区。用户可以轻松贡献内容，无需繁琐设置，只需克隆仓库、创建命名空间、编写代码并提交 pull request。项目强调通过代码内注释捕捉想法和结果，并支持使用表格、图表、markdown 和 hiccup 进行可视化。贡献者可以通过添加 Clojure 命名空间或 markdown 文件来创建文章，并通过 metadata 设置标题、作者、标签等信息。图片也可以添加到命名空间文件夹中，并通过 markdown 显示。完成后，用户提交 pull request，内容经过审核合并后将自动发布到网站。项目还提供实时预览工具，方便用户在编写时查看效果。ClojureCivitas 鼓励开放协作，旨在构建有意义的学习资源网络。

主要讨论点：Clojure内容平台的创新性及其实际应用价值

不同观点：
• **algo_lover**: 认为该平台类似于Medium与org-babel-mode/Jupyter的结合，专注于Clojure内容，执行良好，特别是文学编程的理念。喜欢能够在自己的fork中保留内容副本。但仍在考虑是否值得将内容发布在该平台上，而不是自己的博客。
• **sschmitt**: 提出该平台与Nextjournal的Clerk有何不同，质疑其独特性或创新点。
• **krosaen**: 提到该平台与Devcards相似，暗示可能在功能或用途上存在重叠。
• **oldpersonintx2**: 持批评态度，认为这是对Clojure（最后的类Lisp语言）的又一次无谓的拯救尝试，暗示应放弃这类努力。

补充讨论：
• **algo_lover**对平台的自我内容保存功能表示赞赏，但仍在权衡是否将该平台作为主要的内容发布渠道。
• **sschmitt**和**krosaen**都指出了其他类似工具或平台，提出了对该平台差异化定位的疑问，暗示可能存在功能重复的问题。
• **oldpersonintx2**的观点带有明显的批评和悲观色彩，认为对Clojure的持续维护和开发没有必要，与其他讨论者的态度形成对比。

争议焦点：该平台的独特性及是否值得使用，特别是在已有类似工具（如Clerk和Devcards）的情况下。

Clojure Civitas
Clojure Civitas makes it easy for you to publish Clojure ideas and explorations
without the overhead of setting up a new project, blog, or repo.
Whether you're sketching out a quick experiment or writing a deeper post,
just fork this repo, create a namespace, write, commit and submit a pull request.
This is your shared scratch space.
Think. Code. Share.
⚡ No setup – Clone this repo, make a new namespace, start coding.
✍️ Write as you code – Capture notes, results, and ideas as you go as comments.
🚀 Easy to share – Create a Pull Request, once merged it appears on the
Clojure Civitas Website
.
🧠 Build shared knowledge – Your work becomes part of a community resource.
🧪 Visualize – Your normal REPL workflow, but with tables, charts, markdown, and hiccup.
Rationale
Why markdown in code? We value reproducible artifacts.
See
Clojure Civitas Rationale
.
Contributing
Exploramus, Communicamus, Crescimus
We explore, we share, we grow.
Your perspective matters.
Pull Requests invited, that's the point!
Creating Posts and Pages
Add a Clojure namespace or markdown file in the
/src
folder.
Add metadata on your namespace to set the title, author, and tags.
^{
:kindly/hide-code
true
;
don't render this code to the HTML document
:clay
{
:title
"
About Civitas Metadata
"
:quarto
{
:author
:my-unique-id
:draft
true
;
remove to publish
:type
:post
:date
"
2025-06-05
"
:category
:clojure
:tags
[
:metadata
:civitas
]}}}
(
ns
my.namespace.example
)
Configure your author profile in
site/db.edn
.
Images can be added to the same folder as the namespace,
and displayed with markdown like
;; ![caption](my-image.jpg)
.
The first image on the page is used as a preview in the blog listing,
unless a different image is listed in the metadata.
Kindly
annotations are rendered as visualizations.
^kind/table
{
:tables
[
"
clean layout
"

easy to scan
"

communicates clearly
"
]

build anything

"
]
:many-others
[
"
see the examples
"

creative uses
"
"
visual variety
"
]}
Preview a Webpage
(Optional, Recommended)
Use Clay REPL commands
to visualize the namespace as you write.
When using Clay interactively it renders directly to HTML for speed.
Previewing the Website with Quarto
(Optional, Not Recommended)
The published site goes through a longer process of producing markdown then HTML.
Quarto
is the markdown publishing tool.
clojure -M:clay -A:markdown
quarto preview site
This will open a browser displaying the site locally.
If you would like to preview a single file, then add the path relative to
src
:
clojure -M:clay -A:markdown games/beginning_to_build_a_browser_game.clj
Publish
Create a pull request:
fork the repository
make changes in a new branch and commit them
push the branch to your fork
open a pull request
Your pull request will be reviewed to prevent abuse and then merged.
Once merged, namespaces are automatically published to the website.
Please contact
@timothypratley
if you are having any difficulty submitting a PR.
Check Your Page Views
Publicly available
page view analytics
indicate how widely your idea is being shared.
Editing the Civitas Explorer Database
An open effort to structure learning resources with meaningful connections.
Add to or modify
site/db.edn
.
The goal is to create a database of resources for learning.
See the
explorer
.
Design
Align with Clojure's values: simplicity, community, and tooling that helps you think.
Namespace Selection
A namespace serves as a clear, unique path to its content and follows
Clojure’s naming conventions
.
The namespace should emphasize
what the narrative is about
, not how it is categorized.
Think of it as a logical path that leads to a specific artifact or topic.
Classification elements such as tags, author, document type, level, or publication date belong in
metadata
, not the
namespace.
Start with an organization
if the narrative is about a library or tool maintained by one.
Examples:
scicloj
,
lambdaisland
.
Follow with the specific library or concept.
Examples:
scicloj.clay
,
lambdaisland.kaocha
,
lambdaisland.hiccup
.

data.title: As a linguist, I want to find the words to measure chronic illness
data.author: Avshalom
data.article_summary: 文章由语言学家M Corvi撰写，描述了慢性疾病患者在寻求诊断和表达病痛时的困境。作者讲述了自己在多次求医后，虽然进行了各种测试，但始终缺乏明确的诊断或语言来描述自己的症状，如 mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS) 和 postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS)。作者指出，医学常依赖可观察的现象，但对如疼痛或不适等主观感受缺乏准确的描述和测量方法。作者强调，患者和医生需合作寻找或发明适当的词汇来表达这些“看不见”的感受，并认为定性描述应先于定量测量，以全面了解疾病。文章呼吁对“无形”疾病如长新冠（Long COVID）进行更深入的理解和研究。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：慢性疼痛及功能障碍的描述与测量

不同观点：
• GarnetFloride：强调慢性疼痛与急性疼痛在体验和描述上的不同。慢性疼痛需要围绕疼痛来调整生活，类似于与配偶的关系。疼痛的程度难以用简单的数字衡量，且个体差异显著。举例说明不同情况下疼痛的感知差异，并指出患者希望被相信的诉求。

• rpaddock：分享了因妻子因慢性疼痛自杀而成为倡导者的个人经历，特别提到了颅内低压和氟喹诺酮类抗生素中毒的问题。引入了“勺子理论”来描述慢性病患者的日常活动限制，并建议通过消除饮食中的茄科植物来改善症状。

• PaulKeeble：讨论了用于量化长新冠和慢性疲劳综合症（ME/CFS）功能障碍的Funcap问卷。指出目前测量工具的不足，并强调ME/CFS疲劳的独特性和难以传达性。提出目前尚无被广泛接受的生物标志物。

• user568439：描述了妻子长新冠经历中遇到的医生不重视问题，包括医生不愿进行进一步测试和缺乏对症状触发因素的理解。强调了患者在寻求帮助时遇到的挫折和医生缺乏好奇心和帮助意愿的问题。

• vpribish：认为文章通过个人故事传达了人类代价和内部体验描述的困难。指出当前1-10评分系统的局限性，并提出系统问题的复杂性，包括恶意行为者和 incompetence 的存在。认为改进工具并不一定是明显的“胜利”。

• stared：指出语言的虚拟性与体验的真实性，认为需要更好的方法来命名和测量内部体验。提出利用大型语言模型（LLMs）将个人记录转化为摘要，从而实现更准确的测量。

• captainbland：认为证据比词语更重要，指出慢性条件的症状本身就是证据。提出目标-结果差距的概念，用于解释患者的实际情况，并讨论了在工作和社会中被视为负担的问题。建议可能需要一个新术语如“supportphobia”来描述避免支持的行为。

• onecommentman：提到疑病症（hypochondria）可能影响5%-10%的人口，并指出这可能是医疗成本上升的一个驱动因素。引用了心理学文章来支持这一观点。

• francisofascii：指出不仅是慢性病，任何病毒性疾病都难以描述和找到可靠的生物标志物。患者感觉“不适”、“不活力”，但医疗专业人员可能无法准确判断。

• resource_waste：建议教授维特根斯坦的《逻辑哲学论》和威廉·詹姆斯的实用主义，以帮助理解语言的基础性和科学的有限性。认为这种教育可能有助于培养医生的谦逊和公众的解决方案导向。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多种慢性疼痛和疾病的描述工具和理论，如“勺子理论”和Funcap问卷。
• 强调了语言和测量工具在传达和理解内部体验方面的局限性。
• 提出了医疗系统中存在的医生缺乏好奇心和帮助意愿的问题。
• 指出了社会对科学现实主义的信仰与科学实际能力之间的差距。

44771569.article_content:
Commentary
As a linguist, I want to find the words to measure chronic illness
Written by
M Corvi
–
August 1, 2025
Heather Hogan / The Sick Times
Let me paint a scene that is all too familiar: I’m not feeling well (again), I go to the doctor (again), they take some blood (again; I turn my head away) and poke at me in whatever way my insurance company deems appropriate.
The result is a long sheet of seemingly arbitrary numbers that indicate
something
about my metabolic processes and the resulting sensations, and I leave without much information aside from some variation of: “These tests tell me that your body seems to be functioning the way everyone else’s is. So we leave you linguistically empty-handed, without a diagnosis or words for these sensations. In conclusion, you’re fine.”
Then why do I feel like I’m full of noodles and static electricity? Where’s the electric noodle test, Doc?
If you also have a complex chronic illness, you’re probably familiar with this experience. These conditions and diseases create a massive linguistic gap that can be difficult for patients to bridge — and even more difficult for medical providers because they don’t experience what we do every day in our bodies.
So what words can I, a linguist and a patient with sensations perceivable only to me, use to fully capture these
mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS
) and
postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS)
sensations to my providers?
And, more generally,
how can we measure
our unsettling internal realities if we can’t even name them? How do you effectively measure something like pain, cognitive dysfunction, or feelings of noodliness when so much of medical measurement is reliant on readily observable phenomena — or, stuff that usually has really precise words?
In these moments when I am overwhelmed by this gap, I remind myself that
immaterial to others
doesn’t mean
unreal
— and that, after all, people have words to explain immaterial concepts like gods and quantum physics. The words for these unseeable sensations in my body must exist
somewhere
, and it’s up to patients and healthcare providers to work together to either find or invent them.

My body has always been quick to reject the world. With a family full of medical anomalies, I knew I would one day get my own diagnoses. Growing up, I had seen women in my family suffer from things that were readily dismissed by both clinicians and the general public — namely, chronic pain, fibromyalgia, and migraines. There was never a doubt in my mind that these illnesses caused suffering in the bodies of the people I cared about, even if I couldn’t see or feel the sensations that characterize them.
Eventually, many of these sensations would manifest in my own body. They are bizarre, uncomfortable, and painful sensations that I frequently struggle to find the words for.
I suspected I had MCAS in spring 2019. I began to react strangely to food I’d enjoyed my entire life, had sudden bouts of unexplainable hives, and was often dizzy. To advocate for myself with doctors, I consulted the much-hated “Dr. Google” (that’s
Dr. Google Scholar
to you!). I read any peer-reviewed paper with the right keywords, Wikipedia’d the hell out of any biology I didn’t know, frequented message board after message board, and eventually cobbled together a list of the appropriate tests for my symptoms.
I knew something was wrong with me, and I was determined to articulate it into numerical existence. I eventually did get my diagnosis in March 2022 — which is, comparatively speaking, a very short timeline for receiving a diagnosis of MCAS. I was diagnosed with POTS a few months later after going through a similar gauntlet.
I knew something was wrong with me, and I was determined to articulate it into numerical existence.
Over the course of my diagnoses and ongoing treatment, I’ve internalized a few things about language, illness, and measurement. The first is that, even though it gets easier over time, how I describe the sensations in my body will always be inadequate. That’s not a reflection of me — language can express only so much, and I can’t AirDrop my sensations to another human to make them feel exactly what I’m feeling.
Second, my doctors and I can’t just take a yardstick or thermometer to sensations like pain or discomfort to measure them. Before measuring these sensations in a quantitative, or numerical, way (e.g., a person may be 62 inches tall), we first need a qualitative, or descriptive (e.g. an apple may be green) understanding of what is going on. To get the fullest picture of illness, we need to account for both the quantitative and qualitative — and the qualitative work will always inform the quantitative work.

• resource_waste：建议教授维特根斯坦的《逻辑哲学论》和威廉·詹姆斯的实用主义，以帮助理解语言的基础性和科学的有限性。认为这种教育可能有助于培养医生的谦逊和公众的解决方案导向。

• 讨论中涉及了多种慢性疼痛和疾病的描述工具和理论，如“勺子理论”和Funcap问卷。
• 强调了语言和测量工具在传达和理解内部体验方面的局限性。
• 提出了医疗系统中存在的医生缺乏好奇心和帮助意愿的问题。
• 指出了社会对科学现实主义的信仰与科学实际能力之间的差距。

data.author: kiyanwang
data.article_summary: 根据Stack Overflow 2025年开发者调查，开发者对AI编码工具的信任和依赖显著下降。信任AI输出准确性的开发者比例从2024年的43%降至33%，而愿意将AI工具纳入工作流的开发者比例从72%降至60%。尽管84%的开发者使用或计划使用AI工具，但对其满意度明显降低。专家认为，这种转变源于开发者对AI能力与局限有了更现实的认识，不再盲目信任。许多开发者发现AI在处理已知任务时表现不佳，导致信任度下降。不过，调查也显示开发者正更谨慎地使用AI工具，理解其适用场景，以提高生产力，而非完全放弃。

44795582.article_content:
Trust in AI coding tools is plummeting
According to Stack Overflow's 2025 developer survey.
By
Chris Stokel-Walker
August 04, 2025
You have
1
article left to read this month before you need to
register
a free LeadDev.com account.
A new Stack Overflow survey highlights a steep decline in trust and reliance on AI coding tools, as users get more discerning.
Stack Overflow’s
annual survey of nearly 50,000 developers
acts as a useful benchmark of how software engineers are feeling, and this year’s results suggest a steep decline in sentiment around
AI coding tools
.
This year, 33% of developers said they trust the accuracy of the outputs they receive from AI tools, down from 43% in 2024. At the same time, how favourably developers think of adding AI tools into their workflow fell steeply, from 72% in 2024 to 60% this year.
The 10-plus percentage point swing in both questions was something that stood out to the team behind the survey, too. “One of the most notable trends in this year’s survey is the continued rise in AI tool usage – now at 84% of developers using or planning to use them – contrasted with a clear drop in favourability,” says Erin Yepis, senior analyst for market research and insights at
Stack Overflow
.
Your inbox, upgraded.
Receive weekly engineering insights to level up your leadership approach.
Email address
(Required)
Name
This field is for validation purposes and should be left unchanged.
What’s behind the shift?
Yepis says there are “likely a few forces at play here.” She points out that there was a
gap between the perception of satisfaction
between simple, everyday tasks that devs might do often, and those that they don’t.
“When AI is used for general tasks by those that know what they are looking for, there is not only less room to increase satisfaction, but those tools immediately create a poor experience, too,” she says.
The underwhelming performance of AI at things developers already know how to do is just one indication of why there has been a shift in sentiment. “Developer trust in AI is becoming more realistic as the industry moves beyond the initial hype phase. With increased experience, developers now have a better understanding of AI’s capabilities and limitations,” says Raj Kesarapalli, director at application security company Black Duck.
Kesarapalli says that we might be at that inflection point where developers are starting to utilize AI tools more judiciously, and are similarly considering the way they perform when set to the tasks they’re given. “Ultimately, effective use of AI depends on understanding its strengths and weaknesses and knowing when and how to leverage it,” he says.
More like this
The programming languages facing an AI-driven existential crisis
Kari McMahon
11 generative AI programming tools for developers
Harry Guinness
Hype versus reality
The reality of performance versus hype is why Andrey Korchak, a longtime former chief technology officer, believes we are seeing plummeting trust figures in Stack Overflow’s survey.
“One of the most common stories I hear in 2025 goes like this: someone gives an AI coding agent a try, expecting magic,” he says. “But after a few actions, it messes up the architecture, changes something it shouldn’t, or just spits out bad code.”
At that point, Korchak says, many people might step away from AI, without realizing that the time invested can pay dividends through better prompts or more reasonable expectations.
The answer, for now, is more human oversight of AI outputs to understand
why
AI tools are failing to carry out user requests as intended. Three in four developers who responded to Stack Overflow’s survey say they’ll revert to human oversight when they don’t trust an AI-generated answer.
But there is still a silver lining, says Yepis. “It’s not that developers are abandoning AI – usage is growing, and 69% of the developers using
AI agents
at work agree that productivity is improving,” she says.
Instead, the stats show that developers are using AI more judiciously. “They’re learning
where AI fits in their workflows
– and where it doesn’t,” she says. “That’s a natural progression as a new technology matures: initial enthusiasm gives way to realism, and we’re seeing that shift play out in this year’s results.”

data.title: Build Your Own Lisp
data.author: lemonberry
data.article_summary: 《Build Your Own Lisp》是一本教你使用C语言创建自己的编程语言的书。全书通过1000行代码，引导读者学习C语言并开发一个类似Lisp的语言。书中探讨了Lisp的独特之处，帮助读者提高实际项目开发能力和问题解决技巧，同时写出优雅的代码。该书提供免费在线阅读，也可购买印刷版或电子书以获得更好的阅读体验。许多读者表示，实现自己的Lisp让他们感到成为更完整的C程序员，并认为每个程序员都应尝试这类项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“构建自己的Lisp”及相关资源、工具的讨论

不同观点：
• **赞赏与启发**：[gorgoiler] 对 Iosevka 字体及其相关项目的创造者表示钦佩，认为这些项目极具启发性，能够激励自己努力提升。这种自我驱动的学习过程让他感到振奋。

• **对“构建自己的Lisp”资源的批评**：[cardanome] 认为“Build Your Own Lisp”资源不适合构建可扩展的Lisp，可能会在长期学习中阻碍进步。建议初学者注意这一点，避免养成不良习惯。

• **对资源的扩展理解**：[lskfiep] 认为“Build Your Own Lisp”不仅仅是一个Lisp构建教程，更是一个学习C语言的绝佳资源。它不局限于Lisp的传统特性，而是提供了广泛的实用工具，如解析器库‘mpc’。

• **推荐其他资源**：[staplung] 推荐了Peter Norvig的Python实现的简化Scheme解释器，认为这是一个很好的补充学习资源，适合新手了解Lisp相关概念。

• **历史讨论链接**：[dang] 提供了多个与“Learn C and Build Your Own Lisp”相关的历史讨论链接，展示了这一话题的持续关注度。

• **个人项目分享**：[tnlogy] 分享了自己的自编译Scheme到C编译器项目，并提到受《SICP》一书的启发，询问该书是否仍在课程中使用。

• **对学习过程的反思**：[coderatlarge] 表示对作者免费提供资源感到感激，并分享了自己类似的编码经历。强调了构建测试工具的重要性，并建议参考现有高质量的个人Lisp项目。

• **Lisp比较与应用**：[adz5a] 询问是否存在比较不同Lisp方言（如Lisp 1和Lisp 2）的资源，并讨论了Lisp在LLM（大型语言模型）应用中的潜力。

• **旧工具与语言学习**：[nyrikki] 提到使用纯Lisp Chatlin和C语言学习编程的旧经历，认为即便是简单的语言也能有效学习。

• **多角度实现**：[codr7] 分享了自己从不同角度解决问题的项目，展示了实现语言的不同方法。

• **对教程深度的质疑**：[dark-star] 认为大多数教程在涉及尾调用优化、延续、CPS和Call/CC等高级主题时停止，这些是实现真正实用语言的关键，但构建玩具语言本身也是一个值得追求的目标。

• **对人物形象的建议**：[ale] 认为在讨论构建编译器相关内容时，使用Grace Hopper的肖像比Ada Lovelace更合适。

• **AI生成工具的调侃**：[intellectronica] 幽默地建议可以直接让AI来完成这些工作。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到《SICP》一书，反映出其在编程教育中的经典地位。
• 对不同资源和项目的分享，展现了社区中多种学习和实现路径的多样性。
• 对Lisp在现代应用（如LLM）中的潜力讨论，表明Lisp在当前技术背景下的持续相关性。

data.title: A Carnival Attraction That Saved Premature Babies (2016)
data.author: pr337h4m
data.article_summary: Martin Couney was a renowned figure who ran infant incubator exhibits for over 30 years, most famously at Coney Island. His displays of premature babies in incubators drew large crowds, with an exhibit at the 1933-1934 Chicago World’s Fair being particularly successful. Couney, alongside pediatrician Dr. Julius Hess, cared for premature babies using advanced incubators, despite controversy over the ethics of displaying the infants. Couney claimed to have studied medicine in Europe, but evidence suggests he never officially qualified as a doctor. Despite this, his work saved thousands of babies and influenced American neonatal medicine, eventually gaining recognition as pioneering, though his lack of formal medical credentials remained a point of contention. His collaboration with Hess marked a significant step in gaining legitimacy in the medical field.

44770215.article_content:
Martin Couney holds up Beth Allen, a premature baby who was on view at the Coney Island attraction.
Beth Allen
Nurses in starched white uniforms and doctors in medical coats tended to babies in glass and steel incubators. The infants had been born many weeks premature and well below a healthy birth weight. Stores didn’t make clothes small enough to fit their tiny, skeletal frames so the nurses dressed them in dolls’ clothes and knitted bonnets.
A sign above the entrance read “Living Babies in Incubators” in letters so large they could be read from the other end of the Chicago World’s Fair grounds, which took place over 18 months in 1933 and 1934. The infant incubator exhibit was built at a cost of $75,000 (worth $1.4 million today) and was painted in a patriotic red, white and blue.
The men in charge were leading Chicago pediatrician Dr. Julius Hess and Martin Couney, who was known across America as “the incubator doctor.” Couney was a lugubrious man in his 60s, with thinning gray hair, a mustache and a stoop, something he jokingly attributed to a lifetime of bending over babies. Couney and Hess employed a team of six nurses and two wet nurses.
Martin Couney had run infant incubator exhibits, in which premature babies were displayed to the public, for more than three decades, most famously at Coney Island in New York City. He had long been regarded by desperate parents as a savior, one who offered medical help to babies written off as “weaklings” by mainstream medicine.
But for Hess, who was accustomed to carrying out his work in a more conventional hospital setting, this was a career first.
Miracle at Coney Island: How a Sideshow Doctor Saved Thousands of Babies and Transformed American Medicine (Kindle Single)
More about this product
The exhibit was a hit with the Chicago public who paid 25 cents and flocked by the hundreds of thousands to see the babies.
To celebrate the success of their facility, Couney organized a “Homecoming” celebration on July 25, 1934, for babies who had “graduated” from the incubators at the Chicago’s World’s Fair the previous summer. Of the 58 babies Couney and Hess had cared for in 1933, 41 returned with their mothers for the reunion. The event was broadcast live on local radio and across the fairgrounds.
On the radio program, Couney’s exhibit was portrayed by the announcer not as a frivolous sideshow spectacle, but as an invaluable medical facility:
The Incubator station for premature babies…is not primarily a place of exhibiting tiny infants. Instead, it is actually a lifesaving station, where prematurely born babies are brought from leading hospitals all over the city, for the care and attention that are afforded. The place is spick and span, with doctors and graduate nurses in constant attendance...
Because of the sideshow setting in which he operated, Couney’s career had always been controversial. Many in the medical professional viewed the “incubator doctor” with suspicion, others with outright hostility. The New York Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Children had repeatedly accused Couney of exploiting the babies and endangering their lives by putting them on show.
None of the complaints was sustained, and by the 1930s, Couney was finally being taken seriously as a medical pioneer. Couney’s professional collaboration with Hess marked a key stage in his habilitation.
But while doing research for my radio documentary
Life Under Glass
, which is being broadcast on NPR stations around the country this August, and my book,
Miracle at Coney Island
, I made an incredible discovery about a man who has a claim to have changed the course of American neonatal medicine.
Couney never actually qualified as a medical doctor.
Throughout his career, Couney said he had studied medicine in Leipzig and Berlin. However, I could find no evidence of Couney (or Cohn/Cohen as he was known then) having studied medicine at a university in either city. To become a physician in Germany, one was required to write a thesis. The U.S. National Library of Medicine has copies of the German records: the librarians could not locate a thesis written by Couney.
Couney was deliberately evasive about his date and place of birth. I have discovered that he immigrated to the US in 1888 at 19 years old. But someone of that age would not be old enough to have studied at university in Leipzig and Berlin before going on to do graduate work in Paris at the knee of Pierre Budin, the father of European neonatal medicine, as Couney claimed to have done in numerous press interviews.
In the 1910 U.S. census, Couney listed his career as, “surgical instruments.” Though Couney claimed to be the inventor of an incubator, I have been unable to find any evidence that he registered an incubator patent in the U.S. More likely Couney was a technician. Yet by 1930 he was describing himself in the census as a “physician.”

44770215.article_summary: Martin Couney was a renowned figure who ran infant incubator exhibits for over 30 years, most famously at Coney Island. His displays of premature babies in incubators drew large crowds, with an exhibit at the 1933-1934 Chicago World’s Fair being particularly successful. Couney, alongside pediatrician Dr. Julius Hess, cared for premature babies using advanced incubators, despite controversy over the ethics of displaying the infants. Couney claimed to have studied medicine in Europe, but evidence suggests he never officially qualified as a doctor. Despite this, his work saved thousands of babies and influenced American neonatal medicine, eventually gaining recognition as pioneering, though his lack of formal medical credentials remained a point of contention. His collaboration with Hess marked a significant step in gaining legitimacy in the medical field.

data.article_summary: 文章宣布2025年8月5日是cURL项目发布以来的第10,000天，称为"c10kday"。为了庆祝这一时刻，项目团队邀请用户分享与cURL相关的故事，包括首次使用cURL的经历、cURL如何帮助解决问题的实例以及它对个人工作或生活的意义。这些故事将在cURL的GitHub讨论区收集和分享，虽然团队在持续开发新功能和修复漏洞，但这个日子依然是与社区互动并回顾美好记忆的契机。最后，文章感谢用户对cURL的支持。

From
March 20, 1998
when the first curl release was published, to this day
August 5, 2025
is exactly 10,000 days. We call it the curl-10000-day. Or just
c10kday
. c ten K day.
We want to celebrate this occasion by collecting and sharing stories. Your stories about curl. Your favorite memories. When you used curl for the first time. When curl saved your situation. When curl rescued your lost puppy. What curl has meant or perhaps still means to you, your work, your business, or your life. We want to favor and prioritize the good, the fun, the nostalgic and the emotional stories but it is of course up to your discretion.
We have created this thread in curl’s GitHub Discussion section for this purpose, so please go there and submit your story or read what others have shared.
https://github.com/curl/curl/discussions/17930
In the curl factory this day is nothing special. We keep hammering out new features and bugfixes – just like we always do.
Thanks for flying curl.

data.title: Apache ECharts 6
data.author: makepanic
data.article_summary:
Apache ECharts 6.0 发布了12项重大升级，旨在提升数据可视化的专业性和灵活性。主要改进围绕三个核心维度：

1. **更专业的视觉表现**：
   - 全新默认主题，现代设计语言。
   - 动态主题切换，无需重新初始化图表。
   - 支持暗黑模式，自动适配系统主题。

2. **扩展数据表达边界**：
   - 新增和弦图、蜂群图、散点抖动、断轴等新图表和功能，处理复杂数据场景。
   - 增强股票交易图表，提升标签能力和开箱即用的图表类型。

3. **释放组合自由**：
   - 新的矩阵坐标系，支持像表格一样组合图表和组件。
   - 增强的自定义系列，支持npm发布和动态注册。
   - 新增小提琴图、轮廓图等自定义图表。
   - 优化轴标签布局，防止重叠。

这些升级使ECharts 6.0在数据可视化方面更加强大、可靠和灵活，帮助开发者创造出更具创意的视觉作品。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ECharts库的优缺点及其在不同场景中的应用

不同观点：
• homebrewer：赞赏ECharts的向后兼容性，特别是从其他库（如react-router）迁移过来的体验。其项目从5.6版升级到6.0版仅用了15分钟，且只有图例位置的改变，通过导入旧主题轻松还原。从商业库转到ECharts后没有后悔。
• dev_l1x_be：强调ECharts作为全面的图表解决方案，可以通过特定方法减少包大小，提供了一个链接说明如何操作。
• rorylaitila：认为ECharts总体最佳，快速、完整、易于上手，且具有良好的示例和渲染支持。但抱怨不同图表类型需要不同的数据结构，尤其是数据表功能不够完善和文档不全。
• derkades：对新版本发布感到兴奋，但觉得LLM（大语言模型）相关的描述难以阅读。
• ggregoire：长期使用ECharts，认为其功能齐全，且不像D3那样复杂。特别提到ECharts与React的良好兼容性，其他库往往缺少一些必要的功能（如多Y轴支持）。
• RyanHamilton：三年前评估多个图表框架后选择了ECharts，用于实时数据库可视化，效果极佳，仅有一个未实现的关键功能，现已修复。
• elric：特别喜欢新的和弦图，认为其工具提示和清晰渐变效果出色。
• kakadu：认为ECharts功能不错，但在扩展功能时遇到困难，例如实现甘特图需要深入源码。还提到翻译不够好。
• kylecordes：对ECharts高度赞赏，认为其功能丰富，商业替代品相形见绌。
• porridgeraisin：比较多个前端图表库后，认为ECharts和uPlot最好。最终选择ECharts是因为其动画支持和易用性，特别是与Vue的良好集成。

补充讨论：
• tnolet：询问是否有人从Highcharts切换到ECharts的体验。
• nirav72：询问是否有人使用ECharts进行实时数据的可视化。
• billfruit：询问ECharts是否支持交互式3D图表。

争议焦点：
• 不同用户对ECharts数据结构的复杂性存在争议，尤其是rorylaitila和kakadu提到的图表数据结构不一致和文档不完善问题，与其他用户对ECharts的高度赞赏形成对比。

总的来说，ECharts因其功能全面、易用性和向后兼容性受到广泛好评，但在文档和特定功能的实现上仍有改进空间。

Apache ECharts 6 New Features
Twelve years ago, ECharts was first released on GitHub, planting the seed for an open-source journey.
From a simple charting tool to a visualization powerhouse supporting millions of developers; from a single front-end charting library to a comprehensive technology system covering mobile, large screens, and server-side rendering—over these 12 years, we've witnessed ECharts' continuous technical breakthroughs and have been delighted to see developers worldwide create countless stunning data stories with ECharts.
Now, Apache ECharts 6.0 is officially released, bringing 12 major upgrades to take your data visualization to the next level.
Feature Overview
Twelve years of accumulation, all for more ultimate visual expression. The core strength of Apache ECharts has always come from a deep understanding of developers' real challenges. When defining the direction for 6.0, the question was clear:
How can we make complex data presentation both powerful and elegant?
This drove us to evolve deeply around three core dimensions:
More professional visual presentation
: From a meticulously crafted default theme to intelligent dark mode switching, ensuring charts have a professional look and seamlessly integrate into modern applications.
Expanding the boundaries of data expression
: New chart types and features to handle complex scenarios and enable intuitive expression of deep data.
Unleashing freedom of composition
: From the revolutionary matrix coordinate system to reusable custom series and optimized axis labels—empowering developers to freely compose and turn creativity into unconstrained visual works.
We have made 12 upgrades across these three core dimensions. These are not just simple feature additions, but a solid foundation for building the next generation of data-driven applications. They all point to one goal:
to make ECharts powerful, reliable, and stable in the background, leaving the stage and spotlight for your creative expression.
Below, we introduce these twelve upgrades in detail:
More professional visual presentation
1. Brand New Default Theme
: Modern design language for professional data expression
2. Dynamic Theme Switching
: Seamless runtime theme switching for multi-theme scenarios
3. Dark Mode Support
: Automatically adapts to system dark/light mode for better UX
Expanding the boundaries of data expression
4. New Chord Chart
: Visualize complex relationships and distributions
5. New Beeswarm Chart
: Smartly expand overlapping data points into a honeycomb layout
6. New Scatter Jittering
: Add jitter to scatter plots for better readability of dense data
7. New Broken Axis
: Easily present data with large magnitude differences
8. Enhanced Stock Trading Charts
: Improved label capabilities and more out-of-the-box trading charts
Unleashing freedom of composition
9. New Matrix Coordinate System
: Freely combine chart types and components like a table
10. Enhanced Custom Series
: Support npm publishing and dynamic registration for code reuse
11. New Custom Charts
: Violin, contour, stage, bar range, and line range charts
12. Axis Label Optimization
: Smarter default axis label layout to prevent overflow and overlap
With these upgrades, Apache ECharts 6.0 helps users create more charts more flexibly and conveniently, truly achieving "unlimited possibilities in charting"!
Feature Details
1. Brand New Default Theme
During the development of ECharts 6.0, we analyzed real user scenarios and found that over 70% of developers use the default theme. This made us realize: an excellent default theme should not only be aesthetically pleasing but also meet the general needs of various business scenarios.
The new theme system uses design tokens to reconstruct colors, spacing, and other design elements,
making different chart types and components more harmonious and consistent
.
Although the 6.0 theme has significant changes from 5.x, we provide a
v5.js
theme file for developers who want to use new features but keep the old style for quick migration.
2. Dynamic Theme Switching
In previous versions, changing a chart's theme required disposing of the chart instance and re-initializing, which could negatively impact user experience due to repeated animations. In the new version, we implemented
dynamic theme switching
(see documentation), significantly improving the user experience.
3. Dark Mode Support
With dynamic theme registration and switching, a typical scenario is
listening to the system's dark mode and dynamically adjusting the chart's theme
.

data.title: The Disappearance of Saturday Morning (2003)
data.author: KoftaBob
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：星期六早晨卡通消失的原因和影响

不同观点：
• [simmonmt] 认为《儿童电视法案》（Children's Television Act）及其引入的教育与信息性（E/I）节目可能是导致星期六早晨卡通消失的重要因素，并指出文章遗漏了这一点。他提供了维基百科链接作为参考，强调E/I节目的影响。
• [hackpit] 从个人经历出发，认为限制看电视的时间（如只能在特定时间看电视）也是造成这种文化现象消失的原因之一。他怀念如《Wile E. Coyote》这样的经典卡通，并提到过去孩子们只能在特定时间看电视，随后被要求出去玩耍。
• [JKCalhoun] 描述了自己通过技术手段（Raspberry Pi和自编程序）重建类似童年电视节目表的体验。他强调了现代技术如何帮助重现过去的观看体验，同时指出没有广告和随机填充短片的体验。他还提到自己程序的不足之处以及未来的改进计划。
• [1970-01-01] 认为ATSC 3.0技术和流媒体的普及将很快使非直播广播像AM广播一样消失，预示着传统广播电视的终结。
• [georgeburdell] 对比了2000年代和70、80年代的卡通质量，指出70、80年代也有大量低质量的Hanna-Barbera卡通，质疑文章对卡通质量下降的批评。
• [neuroelectron] 提出担忧，认为如果孩子们不能外出，共享体验（如看卡通）可能成为他们社交的重要途径，而这并不是理想的情况。
• [deadbabe] 从心理时间感的角度分析，认为星期六早晨卡通对孩子们的意义在于它标志着经过漫长学校周后的放松和自由时光，这种期待感增加了卡通的特殊性。

补充讨论：
• [teiferer] 认为文章标题"Disappearance of Saturday Morning"过于宽泛，建议改为更具体的"Disappearance of Saturday Morning Kids Cartoons on TV"，以更准确地反映文章内容和特定受众。
• [throawaywpg] 简单直接地指出，过去的星期六早晨卡通大多只是玩具广告的延伸，质量未必高。

争议焦点：
• 对于导致星期六早晨卡通消失的主要原因，存在不同看法。simmonmt强调法律和E/I节目的影响，而hackpit则关注个人经历和家庭规定的作用。
• 卡通质量的历史对比，georgeburdell质疑文章对2000年代卡通质量下降的批评，认为70、80年代也有大量低质量卡通。

data.title: Weather satellites detect 515-mile-long lightning flash
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 2017年，一场雷暴产生了一道惊人的闪电，长度达515英里（829公里），创下世界纪录。这一巨型闪电（megaflash）从德克萨斯州延伸至密苏里州，打破了2020年创下的477英里（768公里）的纪录。巨型闪电定义为长度至少达到62英里（100公里）的闪电，而普通闪电通常不到10英里（16公里）。研究团队利用GOES-16卫星的数据确认了这一长度。这类巨型闪电非常罕见，通常需要持续约14小时的雷暴才可能产生。随着闪电测绘技术的进步，未来可能会发现更多此类极端现象。研究结果发表在《美国气象学会公报》上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕闪电和距离测量的相关讨论，包括闪电的性质、范围记录以及数据处理问题。

不同观点：
• [hansvm] 认为当前的技术和现象（如电子邮件和闪电）在约500英里的范围内停滞不前，暗示技术或自然现象存在某种限制。链接的文章也讨论了类似的问题。
• [kitd] 关注闪电的机制，特别是图示中正负分支的闪光，猜测是多个放电引发的连锁反应，并询问其他人是否了解其工作原理。
• [Sebb767] 通过将515英里转换为公里和美式足球场的长度来提供一个直观的度量，帮助读者理解距离的实际概念。

补充讨论：
• [ourmandave] 提到木星上出现的宽于地球的雷暴和绿色闪电，引用了相关文章，增加了讨论的趣味性，并将话题扩展到天文和外太空现象。
• [theandrewbailey] 对2017年的闪电打破2020年的记录表示困惑，质疑为何早期事件能超越后期事件，并指出文章中没有解释为何之前的数据未被发现，暗示数据处理可能存在问题。
• [morjom] 关注闪电的具体类型，询问其他人是否知道该闪电是云内闪还是云对地闪，显示出对闪电分类的兴趣。

争议焦点：
• [theandrewbailey] 提出的数据处理问题，质疑为何2017年的闪电记录在2020年之后才被发现，并认为文章没有充分解释这一现象，暗示数据管理和历史记录中可能存在漏洞或不一致。

44768778.article_content:
Some areas are more prone to lightning storms than others.
(Image credit: John finney photography/Getty Images)
It's 2017, and a thunderstorm shoots off a lightning bolt. What's so special about that, you ask? Well, the bolt is an astonishing 515 miles (829 kilometers) long.
Using archival satellite data, researchers just officially confirmed the length of this enormous bolt of lightning that stretched from Texas to Missouri. It sets a new world record, besting the previous title holder — a
477-mile (768-km) bolt from 2020
— by 38 miles (61 km).
"​​We call it megaflash lightning and we're just now figuring out the mechanics of how and why it occurs," Randy Cerveny, an Arizona State University professor who contributed to the study, said in a
statement
.
You may like
When lightning bolts collide, do they unleash powerful gamma-ray flashes?
Watch the sun unleash 600,000-mile-long eruption in fiery outburst (video)
Lightning from above | Space photo of the day for May 23, 2025
Megaflash lightning is defined as a lightning bolt that reaches at least 62 miles (100 km) in length. By comparison, the average lightning bolt measures less than 10 miles (16 km) in length. (Fun fact, most lightning is just an inch or so wide.)
To determine this length of the record-holding megaflash, the team reviewed data from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's
GOES-16 satellite
, which is equipped with a lightning mapper that observes about one million bolts per day. Their analysis determined the true length of the bolt: a whopping 515 miles.
So, how exactly does one measure a megaflash? Previously, researchers used ground-based radio networks to track lightning bolts. However, satellites with lightning mappers are updating the process.
GOES-16 satellite image recording a record-setting 515-mile ligtning megaflash during a storm in October 2017. Red circles mark positively charged branches of the lightning, and blue circles mark negatively charged branches.
(Image credit: NOAA)
"Adding continuous measurements from
geostationary orbit
was a major advance," Michael Peterson of Georgia Tech Research Institute, who served as lead author of a paper on the study, said in the statement. "We are now at a point where most of the global megaflash hotspots are covered by a geostationary satellite, and data processing techniques have improved to properly represent flashes in the vast quantity of observational data at all scales."
Get the Space.com Newsletter
Breaking space news, the latest updates on rocket launches, skywatching events and more!
Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands
Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors
Megaflashes like these are quite rare — less than one percent of thunderstorms produce them. Typically speaking, the thunderstorms that indeed manage to produce them must be churning for 14 hours or more, covering an area at least the size of the state of New Jersey, per Peterson's research.
RELATED STORIES
—
ISS astronauts spot lightning strike from space
—
Was life on Earth sparked by cloud-to-ground lightning strikes?
—
Most powerful gigantic jet lightning bolt ever
Those conditions aren't altogether
that
rare, to be fair. And, as our lightning-mapping satellites collect new data, we'll probably start noticing even more megaflashes. "It is likely that even greater extremes still exist, and that we will be able to observe them as additional high-quality lightning measurements accumulate over time," said Cerveny,
A paper on the research was published in the
Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society
.

community@space.com.

Contributing writer
Space.com contributing writer Stefanie Waldek is a self-taught space nerd and aviation geek who is passionate about all things spaceflight and astronomy. With a background in travel and design journalism, as well as a Bachelor of Arts degree from New York University, she specializes in the budding space tourism industry and Earth-based astrotourism. In her free time, you can find her watching rocket launches or looking up at the stars, wondering what is out there. Learn more about her work at
www.stefaniewaldek.com
.

data.title: More than two hard disks in DOS
data.author: yuhong
data.article_summary:
本文探讨了Microsoft OS/2 1.21磁盘驱动程序的异常行为，并追溯到Compaq的EXTDISK.SYS驱动程序。研究发现，DOS 5.0之前的版本不支持超过两个由BIOS暴露的硬盘，若硬盘过多，系统可能会在启动时挂起。这一问题源于早期PC硬件限制，当时大多数电脑由于物理空间和电源限制，无法安装超过两个全高5¼英寸硬盘。

Compaq和Adaptec在1988年左右分别推出了支持更多硬盘的解决方案。Compaq通过不通过BIOS暴露额外硬盘，而是通过EXTDISK.SYS驱动让DOS用户访问。Adaptec则通过其AHA-154x SCSI卡和ASPI驱动解决该问题。

DOS 5.0之前版本的bug导致系统无法处理超过两个硬盘，具体表现为MS-DOS内核在计算文件系统参数时进入无限循环。该问题在DOS 2.0到4.0版本中普遍存在，直到DOS 5.0才得以解决。

主要讨论点：早期PC硬件限制导致硬盘数量受限的问题

不同观点：
• [blueflow] 认为早期主板通常只有一个IDE/平行ATA端口，每个端口只能支持两个可寻址驱动器（主驱动和从驱动）。如果有第二个ATA端口，则最多只能支持四个驱动器。这是硬件限制导致的，并解释了启动时屏幕上显示的"primary master"文本的来源。

• [mikeytown2] 指出，带有IDE端口的声卡用于连接CD-ROM驱动器在当时也是很常见的配置。

• [philipstorry] 表示对早期硬件配置的怀念，并提到自己在Windows 7和SATA时代之前很少使用超过2个固定磁盘。他进一步解释了IDE和SATA之前的硬盘配置情况，通常只有两个控制器，每个控制器支持两个设备。他还提到如果需要更多磁盘，可以使用SCSI，但SCSI支持在PC上的表现不佳，可能让人选择UNIX工作站。

补充讨论：
• [tempodox] 以幽默的方式质疑，如果640KB的内存已经足够，那么要那么多硬盘干什么，暗示早期PC的硬件需求和现代需求的不同。

• 争议的焦点在于早期PC硬件的限制是否真的导致了一些技术问题未被发现。具体来说，是否因为早期硬件配置的限制（如硬盘数量）使得某些软件问题未被及时发现和解决。

• 另一个潜在的争议点是SCSI在早期PC中的表现问题，有人认为SCSI提供了更多磁盘支持但表现不佳，可能影响用户选择更专业的计算平台如UNIX工作站。

44796698.article_content:
Investigating the rather odd behavior of the
Microsoft OS/2 1.21 disk driver
led me to
Compaq and their EXTDISK.SYS driver
. While experimenting with various setups, I realized that DOS versions older than 5.0 do not support more than two hard disks exposed by the system’s BIOS, and will in fact quite likely hang early during boot-up if there are “too many” hard disks.
This seems to have been one of the many things that “everyone knew” back in the day, similar to the fact that DOS versions older than 3.3 may
hang while booting
from disks with significantly more than 17 sectors per track.
As was the case with the “too many sectors per track” problem, the issue with “too many hard disks” was missed for years simply because no one had a PC with more than two hard disks. This was a technical rather than architectural limitation. While the IBM PC/XT and PC/AT BIOS implementations were limited to two hard disks, the INT 13h interface as such was not.
In the days of full-height 5¼” drives, it simply was not feasible to install more than two hard disks into a PC, especially when a 5¼” floppy drive was also required. Even the big IBM PS/2 Model 80 (1987) with a tower case could only house two full-height 5¼” drives. There might also be trouble with the power supply, as the PC hard disks of the time were not designed for staggered spin-up and a standard AT power supply might have trouble spinning up four drives at the same time.
Sure, there were half-height hard disks, but who wanted four drives in the first place? People who needed to maximize the storage capacity… and the most obvious way to do that was buying a large capacity drive, which in the 1980s was inevitably a full-height 5¼” monster. Like my
1988-model 650 MB ESDI drive
, for example.
Yes, there were solutions like the NetWare DCB which supported many drives, but those were only usable by NetWare and did not expose the drives via INT 13h.
Two things happened circa 1988. One was Compaq releasing the Deskpro 386/25 with an expansion unit option, a system which supported up to four hard AT-style disks (that is, the expansion unit housed up to two ESDI drives accessible via the PC/AT hard disk style programming interface, which may be called WD1003 or WD1010 or several other things). The other development was Adaptec releasing the AHA-1540/1542 SCSI HBA, and there were perhaps other SCSI vendors as well.
Compaq supported up to four hard disks, Adaptec in theory up to seven. In any case, it is apparent that both companies ran into the same problem with DOS, and solved it in a very similar manner.
Compaq simply did not expose the drives in the expansion unit through the BIOS at all. DOS users needed the EXTDISK.SYS driver, and users of other operating systems (such as OS/2 or NetWare) needed a custom driver.
Adaptec was in a more complicated situation. The AHA-154x was an add-on card which could be installed in a PC/AT compatible machine (the AHA-154x did not work in older systems because it was a bus-mastering adapter) that already had one or two AT style drives. The AHA-154x BIOS keeps the total hard disk maximum to two. In practice that means that if there are two SCSI hard disks attached to an AHA-154x (which also includes AHA-154xA and AHA-154xB, but not necessarily newer models), the Adaptec BIOS may add zero, one, or two drives to the system, depending on how many hard disks there are already installed. In any case, the total won’t be greater than two.
For DOS users, Adaptec offered a combination of ASPI4DOS.SYS (ASPI driver for the AHA-154x) plus ASPIDISK.SYS (DOS hard disk device driver). Adaptec’s ASPIDISK.SYS was functionally very similar to Compaq’s EXTDISK.SYS and allowed DOS users (especially users of DOS 4.x and older) to utilize more than two hard disks.
DOS Bug
The bug is quite visible in the MS-DOS 4.0 source code. In MSINIT.ASM (IO.SYS/IBMBIO.COM module), DOS
calls INT 13h/08h
and stores the number of disks in the HNUM variable. No attempt is made to validate the value returned by INT 13h.
Further down in MSINIT.ASM, DOS
sets up the hard disks
, calling the SETHARD routine for each drive, but it will not set up more than two. Trouble will start near the
SETIT label
, where the DRVMAX variable may end up with a number much higher than the number of drives that SETHARD was run on.
Eventually, disaster strikes in the $SETDPB routine in the DOS kernel. The
code near LOG2LOOP label
attempts to calculate the cluster shift for the FAT file system, but gets stuck in an endless loop because the BPB for a drive was never initialized and contains zeros.
This bug is present in every DOS version with hard disk support before 5.0, that is, in DOS 2.0 up to and including DOS 4. In my experiments, all these DOS versions hang when booting on a machine that exposes four BIOS drives. MS-DOS 4.01 from April 1989 still hangs, and so does Russian MS-DOS 4.01 from February 1990.
It is clear that the bug went unnoticed or at least unfixed for a number of years simpl
